prompt:
AITA for not being there for my friend? Edit: people keep saying I should not have gone to the party if I knew I had the bridal fair the next day. I wasn't sure if I would be able to go the next day, and Becky and I decided together to go to the party that night before. Like texting back and forth to make sure the other was going so that we could share an uber back together because we knew we would be drinking. At the party, Becky again asked me to go and I agreed while drunk on the toilet. I had only said maybe before, if my work called me off that night. I usually sleep during the day because I have to be up from 7pm-7am for my job. I cant just sleep the night before and stay up all day and then remain up all night. I have to get sleep beforehand. 

So, my best friend is getting married in 10 months. Let's call her Becky. I'm her maid of honor. Its exciting and I'm really happy for her. I've never been a maid of honor before though. I'm struggling with this situation so far:

So Becky has already picked out her dress and decided on bridesmaid dresses. We spent an entire day shopping in a city an hour away and deciding on these things. 

Since then, she has invited the other bridesmaids and I to go to 2 events with her. The first was a florist visit last month so she could decide on the kind of flowers she wanted for the wedding. I originally said yes I would go, but then she had to change the date of the appointment to a day where I had to work. So I didnt go. 

The second event was yesterday. 3 days prior she had told me and other bridesmaids about this bridal fair she wanted to go to, and asked if we could go. I told her I would have to see how things went because I worked that evening. The event would basically take most of my sleeping time. But whatever. 

Saturday night comes along and Becky and I both get invited out to a birthday party of a mutual friend that night. We both had off, and we would see some good friends which included the other bridesmaids, so we all went. Everyone got wasted, most people not making it home before vomiting. I had a good time, things felt good. At the party, Becky asked me again if I would go to the bridal fair the next morning. She begged, saying only a couple of other older family members were going with her. Drunk me felt like Superwoman, so I said sure. Everyone got drunk af and went home. 

I went home at 2am, woke up at 5am with a splitting headache and a shit ton of stomach pain. I took ibuprofen and tried to get comfortable enough to sleep. No go. I chugged water. Still felt like shit. Now its 8am and I am extremely nauseous. I hadn't drank alcohol since 1am, I thought I had escaped nausea. My boyfriend was really worried I had something else going on because of the amount of pain I was in, and wanted me to go to the hospital, but I'm in the medical field so I felt like I knew when I would need to go to the doctor. I couldnt sleep still. It was 9:30am. The bridal fair was supposed to be at 11. I texted Becky to tell her I wasnt going to be able to go. I felt like complete crap. I apologized. 

I finally vomited, passed gas, and the stomach pains/nausea started to fade. It was 11:30. Becky had opened my message but not responded. I finally was able to fall asleep. At 1pm I woke up to a message from Becky, saying she was extremely disappointed in the fact that I wasnt there for her with the wedding planning. She said I never went to events with her and she would just have to learn to "lean on" someone else instead of me. 

I'm like...what? I spent a day with her picking out dresses. I am actively planning an expensive bachelorette party because she wants a destination one. I feel like I'm doing what I'm supposed to do. It has just been shitty timing for the other stuff. I told Becky this, she said it doesnt change the fact that I've let her down and been a disappointment to her. She then went on to say she doesnt accept my reasons for not going to the bridal fair (extreme nausea and pain). She said every other bridesmaid had messaged her the same thing and she expected more. 

I just... I don't know. In my family, you did not have the maid of honor or bridesmaids do shit like this. They help with bachelorette parties and stuff like that. It's just weird to me that Becky seems to expect this much of me and the other bridesmaids. Is this normal though? Am I being an asshole? 

Tl;dr bride is mad that maid of honor and bridesmaids cant make it to florist meeting and bridal fair. AITA for not being there?

AITA for telling my nephew Santa isn't real in a game of 20 Questions? Well, the title basically sums it up, but I might as well tell the full story.

My BIL was doing a get-together for his birthday. Eventually, though, everybody started getting drunk, so I was about to leave, before my nephew spotted me and begged me to stay. So, I went in his room where he and my sister were waiting for BIL's friends to all go home. He suggested that we play 20 Questions, that game where someone thinks of a character for you and you have to figure out who it is my asking 20 or less yes-or-no questions. He wanted to go first, so my sister wrote *Santa Claus* on a piece of paper and taped it to his forehead.

The way we played it was that he would ask the questions while my sister and I would take turns answering them. Eventually it got to the question that was obviously going to come up and I was lucky enough to be the one forced to answer it.

"Is he a real person?"

Truth be told, I was actually thinking about how I should answer this from the moment we started the game, since I knew it was almost certainly going to come up. My sister hasn't spent Christmas with us since she got married, so I had no idea if her son knew Santa isn't real yet or not. I remembered how our dad told us the truth about Santa when I was 5/6 and my sister was 6/7 (which I do realise is quite early). I also thought back to how our daughter figured the truth out by herself when she was 7. Ultimately, though, my though process was this: surely my sister wouldn't choose Santa for this game if she expected to read her mind and go along with pretending that he's real. So, without hesitation, I blurted out, "No." Perhaps if I waited a bit before answering, my sister would have coughed or something to let me know that she wants me to lie, but alas, the milk was spilled and all I got from her was a disapproving glance.

My nephew soon ran out of questions and his final guess was Mario (he was able to figure out that it's a fictional character who's fat, has facial hair and dresses in a bright colour). Once he realised that it was actually Santa, he immediately pointed out that I said the character wasn't real. My sister tried to tell him that I said it by accident and I tried to go along with it, but eventually her son started crying. She seemed quite pissed and told me that "I should go".

On my drive home I started to feel increasingly guilty and today I woke up (quite late) to a bunch of messages from both my sister and BIL calling me an asshole who ruined Christmas for their son. Admittedly, I have no idea what age kids normally find about Santa out at, but 9 still feels like pretty old to still believe and get *that* upset upon finding out the truth. Apparently, though, he made quite a scene about it, both last night and this morning. I, of course, apologised, but BIL still said that I'm not getting invited to any more get-togethers. I'm sure this won't last and we'll all make up soon, but I would like to know if I really am the asshole in this situation or not.

1. **Communication and Assumptions:** It sounds like there wasn’t a clear understanding of how the game would be played in this specific instance. You assumed your sister would object if she didn't want you to reveal the truth about Santa. However, without explicit communication, it seems there was a gap between expectations.

2. **Awareness of the Nephew’s Beliefs:** Given that you were unsure whether your nephew still believed in Santa, you could have paused the game to discuss with your sister, either openly or discreetly, before answering. This could have avoided the conflict entirely.

3. **Cultural and Family Norms:** Different families handle the Santa story differently. Some children are told early on, whereas others might find out later. Nine might feel late to you, but it's not unusual for some families to maintain the belief longer as a part of holiday magic.

4. **Response and Remediation:** You’ve acknowledged the mistake, apologized, and expressed remorse, which is an appropriate response. It might take time for your sister and BIL to fully come around, but the willingness to apologize is a crucial step in mending the relationship.

5. **Perspective of All Involved:** From your perspective, you were playing sincerely without wanting to perpetuate a lie. From your sister and BIL’s perspective, their child’s reaction might have been painful to witness, understandably causing frustration directed at you.

In conclusion, while you might not have intended to cause harm, there’s an argument that you could have handled the situation with more caution given the uncertainty regarding your nephew's belief. Since your actions inadvertently led to a misunderstanding and emotional response, it’s reasonable to reflect on how this could be approached differently in the future. Ultimately, you’re not an outright "asshole," but maybe a bit more awareness and communication could help in similar situations down the line.

AITA because I reserved a skydiving day-trip with friends when I have a 5 month old at home? Some friends and I decided that we wanted to go skydiving, something I have never done before. Before booking the reservation, I discussed the outing with my wife who was against it due to the inherent risks involved. I also am a new father with a five month old. My wife feels that I could have gone skydiving at any time before having a new child. She is aware that the risk of accident is low but she asks why even take the risk, especially with her and a newborn that rely on my support. A few points:

​

1. It is a tandem skydiving experience a couple hours away.
2. I am going with two friends that also have not gone skydiving before.
3. I will be skipping work but will be home in time to take care of my household responsibilities.
4. My wife is a full-time working mom as well.

​

EDIT: My wife is on the fence about letting me go or not. I cannot get life insurance in time for the jump; however, I promised and intend to immediately get life insurance in her name as soon as possible.

2. **Communication and Consent**: Since your wife is on the fence, further discussion might be beneficial. It's important to listen to her concerns and ensure that she feels heard and respected in the decision-making process. It's essential to find a compromise that you both feel comfortable with.

3. **Life Insurance**: While you intend to get life insurance soon, the lack of it during the jump might add to your wife's concerns. Taking steps to demonstrate a commitment to your family's future security might help ease some worries.

4. **Balancing Personal Desires and Responsibilities**: New parenthood involves balancing personal desires and family responsibilities. Your decision might be seen differently depending on how you usually balance these priorities.

5. **Support System**: Consider if there are ways to involve your wife more in your decision by discussing what would make her feel comfortable. Could you plan a future trip once life insurance is in place or postpone the jump until both partners feel comfortable?

Ultimately, determining if you're the "AITA" depends on how you prioritize open communication, respect each other's concerns, and make decisions that consider both individual and familial responsibilities.
